title: Friction Catalogue
eyebrow: Design · every known point where house-rules makes your work harder, and one order to fix them in

short.lead: The plugin is meant to save your effort, and right now it costs you effort in six places. This page lists each one, from three sources: what went wrong in this session, the 226 issues open on GitHub today (counted with gh issue list), and the traps already written in the docs. Many open issues describe the same problem more than once (pictures in pages has three, approvals that don't register has five), and most are labelled "in progress" with no work under way. The proposal is to stop adding one-off fixes, fix the six areas in order, one feature each, and close the duplicates as each area lands. The session handoff work pauses until area 5, because it can't be tested for real before then.
short.hint: Tap an area to see what goes wrong, the issues that already describe it, and what done looks like.
items: cross
Area 1
Approvals that look right register nothing

Today alone, five messages meant as approvals moved nothing: "Handoff overwrite design 1A", "Handoff overwrite design approved 1A", "Handoff overwrite 1A 2A" (which the page's own copy box gave you), "Send it" (a button I offered, which sends only its label), and a build plan approval refused because the loop missed issues I had opened. Open issues on the same problem: #491 (word order and copy box), #481 (an approval moves only what you named), #475 (the loop counts every issue opened during Plan), #429 (approvals ignored in cloud sessions), #379 (approvals ignored from the Claude app), #296 (approvals dropped when the folder isn't a repo).
Done when every way you naturally approve, including a reply button, moves the stage or says plainly why not, and the plugin never offers you a line or a button that won't work.
cross
Area 2
The code lock costs a round trip for every small fix

"skip design" lets one file edit through, so a fix plus its test needs two unlocks. A fault found in QA needs a whole new design, plan and approval before a one-line fix, which happened twice today. Open issues: #480 (ways around the code lock), #484 (shell writes outside Build), #459 (a question mid-build locks code).
Done when a fix found in QA goes back to Build with one message from you, and "skip design" covers one change across its files, not one edit.
cross
Area 3
The guard refuses routine, safe commands

Today it refused the pickup's own restore command, every git command run in another folder with cd or -C, a read-only script that named the stage file, and a third run of a check script. Open issues: #478 (stop the guard refusing routine commands), #465 and #467 (rerun limit counts reading a script as running it), #203 and #192 (commits prompt after a cd), #134 and #136 (helpers stall on approvals), #200 and #198 (refusing instead of asking).
Done when the guard refuses only what can't be undone, and every refusal names a way forward that works.
cross
Area 4
Pages lose their pictures and their copy box

Pictures break once a page is published or opened elsewhere, in every repo. Copy my reply has failed in the app's browser pane, and gave you a line the loop rejects. A small wording change costs an editor pass, then a phrase check, then another rebuild. Open issues: #490, #462 and #313 (pictures), #464 and #335 (copy box), #466 and #377 (the builder accepts broken pages), #419 to #424 (the builder refuses a page missing what it owes).
Done when every page shows its pictures and its copy box works wherever it is opened, and a page the builder accepts passes every later check.
cross
Area 5
A build can't be tested where you use it

Installs come from main, so a branch's changes reach the desktop app, cloud sessions and other accounts only after a merge. Today's desktop test needed throwaway clones with hand-written settings, and the desktop app ran your installed copy of the plugin alongside the test copy anyway. Cloud sessions couldn't be started from here at all. Open issues: #179 (cloud environments install the plugin), #438 (plugin dependencies proven together). The session handoff (#406 and #488) waits here: its QA needs the desktop app, a cloud session and a second account.
Done when one command points the desktop app and cloud sessions at a branch build and back again, with nothing else running beside it, and the session handoff passes QA on all three surfaces.
cross
Area 6
226 open issues, many stale or duplicated

Two full sets of "QA evidence" issues (#389 to #395 and #411 to #417), three picture issues, five approval issues, and dozens labelled "in progress" with no work under way. The end-of-turn checks read these labels, so stale ones cause wrong reminders and refusals.
Done when every open issue is either real remaining work or gone. I propose the closes as one list you approve, so nothing is closed without you.
check
Partly fixed
Already on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff

The pickup's restore command now uses git apply and leaves out the stage file (commit d62be1a). The design page for the handoff overwrite, pictures and approvals is approved, and issues #488 to #491 are open. Those carry into areas 1, 4 and 5 rather than being built separately.
Nothing from you.

You decide
The order, and what happens to the open issues
you
Question 1 below asks the order; question 2 asks how the duplicates are handled.
Choose one option in each question.

choices: q1
1. In what order are the areas fixed?
A
Approvals, code lock, guard, pages, testing on real surfaces, then the issue cleanup

Each area makes the next one cheaper: once approvals register and the lock is proportionate, every later fix costs you one message instead of several. Testing on real surfaces comes after the plugin stops getting in the way, and the handoff finishes there. Cleanup comes last, because each area closes its own duplicates as it lands.
B
Issue cleanup first, then the same order
A clean list first makes the rest easier to follow and stops stale labels causing wrong reminders, but nothing you feel day to day changes until the second area starts.
C
Finish the session handoff first, then the areas in order
The handoff is closest to done, but its remaining QA needs area 5, so finishing it first means more throwaway clones and hand-written settings.
Each area is one feature: one design page, one build plan, built and checked before the next starts.
q2
2. What happens to the issues that describe the same problem?
A
Each area starts by folding its issues into one, and proposes the rest for closing

When an area starts, its design page lists every open issue it covers. On approval, one issue carries the work, and the others are put on a close list you approve, with each one pointing at the issue that replaced it. Nothing is closed without you.
B
Leave the existing issues and open new ones per area
Nothing old is touched, but the list keeps growing and the stale labels keep causing wrong reminders.
Either way, no issue is closed without your approval.

wrapup.summary: A catalogue of the six areas where house-rules costs you effort, and one order to fix them in.
wrapup.changing: Only this page. No code is written, and nothing is closed, until you approve.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick of one option in each of questions 1 and 2, or what you want changed.
